title: Quantization — fewer bits, same answers
intro: Model sizes double yearly. GPU memory doesn't. Bits are the lever.

steps.title: Fewer bits per number
steps.body: Like storing **π as 3.14** instead of 3.14159 — for 70 billion numbers. Models ship in BF16 (2 bytes/param); quantization stores them in FP8, INT8, or INT4. The embedding layer and LM head stay high-precision to protect accuracy; the seven linear layers per block — where the parameters actually live — get compressed.

viz.title: Bits → gigabytes
viz.caption: Llama 4 Scout: 220 GB at BF16 (3 GPUs) → 55 GB at 4-bit (one card).

steps.title: Two schemes, two bottlenecks
steps.body:
**W8A16** quantizes *weights only*: compressed weights stream HBM→SRAM (half the data — a **latency** win), then dequantize to BF16 for the math. **W8A8** also quantizes *activations*, so the matmuls run on low-precision tensor cores (H100 FP8: 2× the BF16 FLOPS) — a **latency AND throughput** win.

⚠️ The classic trap: this is a **performance** distinction, *not* an accuracy one. Calibrated, both preserve quality.

steps.title: Calibration is the magic
steps.body:
Blind rounding degrades — especially at 4-bit. Calibrated methods run a few hundred representative samples through the model to learn what to protect:

- **AWQ** — *not all weights are equal*: shields weights tied to large activations, compresses the rest hard. Lighter; the INT4 favourite.
- **GPTQ** — *compensate for error*: Hessian-based sensitivity, layer-by-layer quantization, remaining weights nudged to offset rounding error. Industry standard.
- **SmoothQuant** — flattens activation spikes; the W8A8 INT8 pick.

steps.title: Proof it holds up
steps.body: Published averages (pass@1 over AIME 2024 / MATH-500 / GPQA-Diamond) for Qwen-14B — quantized bars sit on top of the baseline:

viz.title: Accuracy: BF16 vs quantized

points.label: BF16
points.note: Baseline: 73.6 average. Full precision, full size.

points.label: W4A16
points.note: 4-bit weights, ~4× smaller: 72.8 — a 0.8-point dip for a quarter of the memory.

points.label: FP W8A8
points.note: 8-bit weights+activations, 2× smaller: 74.3 — ABOVE baseline, i.e. run-to-run noise.

viz.caption: A real RAG workload (Llama-3-70B, 2×H100, FP16→FP8) tripled throughput: ~158 → ~474 tok/s.

recap: Quantization trades precision for size — and buys **bandwidth** (weights) and **compute** (activations). W8A16 vs W8A8 is about *which bottleneck you speed up*, never about accuracy loss. Calibration (AWQ/GPTQ/SmoothQuant) is what keeps recovery near 99% — check the model card, per benchmark.
